claims.text: etcd is the key-value store backing all cluster data; of the cluster's components only the API server reads and writes it directly (docs: only the API server and backup tooling need access).
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Overview > Components (etcd); Cluster Architecture

claims.text: Other components (kube-scheduler, kubelets, controllers) and kubectl read and change cluster state only through the API server.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Communication between Nodes and the Control Plane; The Kubernetes API

claims.text: kube-scheduler watches for newly created Pods with no assigned node and selects a node for them to run on; it binds the Pod to the node through the API server and does not run the Pod itself.
The kubelet is an agent on each node; it makes sure containers described in Pods assigned to its node are running, and reports Pod and node status to the API server.
Kubernetes controllers are control loops that watch the state of the cluster and make or request changes to move the current state closer to the desired state.
kube-controller-manager runs the built-in controllers (control loops) of Kubernetes.

In a kind cluster, kube-apiserver, etcd, kube-scheduler and kube-controller-manager run as static Pods named <component>-<node> on the control-plane node in kube-system; the kubelet runs as a systemd service on each node. RESTARTS/AGE vary.
claims.source_hint: outputs/stage-2/scripts/k8s/control-plane.txt; kubernetes.io: Static Pods (kubeadm control plane); kind node image (systemd kubelet)

claims.text: kubectl get pods --field-selector spec.nodeName=<node> lists only Pods assigned to that node; kubectl get pod -o wide adds IP, NODE, NOMINATED NODE and READINESS GATES columns.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Field Selectors (spec.nodeName for Pods); kubectl get -o wide; outputs/stage-2/scripts/k8s/control-plane.txt

claims.text: On donhang-control-plane, kube-system also runs coredns (2), kindnet and kube-proxy Pods; these provide cluster DNS and networking.
claims.source_hint: outputs/stage-2/scripts/k8s/control-plane.txt; kubernetes.io DNS for Services; kind kindnet

claims.text: Because the control-plane node carries the NoSchedule taint, kube-scheduler places web on donhang-worker or donhang-worker2; output masks which one.
A Pod can already have spec.nodeName set (shown in NODE) while its container is still being created (STATUS ContainerCreating), since scheduling precedes the kubelet starting containers.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Pod Lifecycle (Pending: scheduled, images downloading); kubectl get -o wide

claims.text: kubectl get pod web -o yaml returns the object as stored by the API server: metadata (name), spec (desired state) and status.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Objects In Kubernetes (spec and status); kubectl get -o yaml

claims.text: scripts/k8s/control-plane.sh@stage-2 lines 11-17: kubectl get pods -n kube-system --field-selector spec.nodeName=donhang-control-plane, then kubectl get pod web -o wide.

kube-scheduler and the kubelet each repeatedly compare stored desired state with reality and act (scheduler: Pods without a node; kubelet: Pods bound to its node without running containers), i.e. work as control loops.
